message.content: Lions (family Felidae, order Carnivora) and zebras (family Equidae, order Perissodactyla) do not share a recent common ancestor at the species or genus level. Their most recent common ancestor is a small, early placental mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, during the Paleogene period, and belongs to the clade **Laurasiatheria**. This ancestor would have been a generalized, small-bodied mammal that gave rise to the lineages leading to modern carnivorans (like lions) and perissodactyls (like zebras).
